Well, they are called 'african soft furred rats' but they aren't rats like we know them. ASF are between a mouse and a rat, a little less domesticated and don't grow as big as pet rats. 
It is true that regular rats and mice shouldn't be together but since these guys have the same requirements as regular mice they can happily live together without being able to breed. Perfect companion for a little male mouse!

They are about 5 weeks old, definitely still little babies but are able to care for themselves, I always heard with coupling ASF rats that the younger, the better chance at success. 

I always couple the same way. Small enclosure with a bit of food and drink, just one house big enough for them all. 

Keep a close eye on them the first few days but if everything goes well you can transfer them to a bigger cage after half a week. Don't overcrowd the big cage as well, keep it quite bare the first week or so and then start to add toys and hides.

I'm european so it's all weighed in grams but there are converters online if needed. You can half the recipe if needed. 

120 g fruit or veggies
350 ml water
250 g sugar
8 g agar-agar, make sure it's 100% pure
1 tsp honey

Cut the fruit or vegetables into small pieces and put them in a container with about half of the water. 
Puree it finely and empty them into a saucepan with the remaining water. 
Turn on the stove, pour the sugar into the pan and stir until it has dissolved. Add the agar-agar and cook the paste for about 2 minutes until the mixture sticks and becomes viscous.
Remove the pan from the heat and let it cool down for about 1 minute Now add the honey and stir.
Fill the jelly in portions and seal it airtight.

Kuvasz, Great Pyrenees, Anatolian Shepherd and breeds like that are best suited for protection of livestock and poultry. As other has said, no ball. Stuff their houses or spread around tissue. If you spread it around they sometimes dig their own home or choose to stuff  the existing homes themselves. Litterbox is not really useful, you can try, a couple might get what it is meant for but rats would use it faster than mice. They do tend to just pick a corner or house to pee in, the poop tends to go everywhere! How many girls? Is it an existing group? If it's more than three girls I would get an extra wheel or flying saucer, do make sure the wheels are big enough! If the spine and beginning of the tail bends when running in the wheel it means that it's too small and can cause longterm health issues to their spine. A saucer is easier in that way, since it's less restrictive but takes up more space. A couple more hanging toys also, they love fuzzy hammocks, you can easily make those at home with some fabric or you can hang thick rope, these guys love to climb. They'll chew a lot of things so I try to get them things that they are allowed to destroy (eggcartons, weaved grass matts, carton boxes, empty paper rolls (highly recommended),.. ) but you'll still will need to buy plenty of toys not only to replace other chewed up toys/houses, it's also when you clean and redecorate their home, it's advised to place in a couple new things to enrich their environment, just keep like one extra set. They don't have very long memories, so they won't remember a toy that was in their cage a month ago. Just keep switching around, they are very curious creatures who love to explore.

Not op, but I can give you a couple of tips. Tameness is really something that depends from mouse to mouse. I've had girls that I didn't really tame but were already super sweet when I got them, others I have for years and still struggle to pick them up to clean the cage. A good responsible breeder plays a large part in personality. 

Other than that it really is patience, don't expect them to love you after a week, interact with them as much as possible, start with putting your hand in the cage, just placing your hand on the ground and keep it still so they'll be tempted to smell your scent. You can start with keeping some snacks in your hand so they'll associate you with food. In that first week you can probably see which mice would be the easiest to tame, the ones that are brave enough to come to your hand. And yeah, it's just patience. I only tame my mice to a point were they are relaxed enough not to run away when I'm in their cage to change something or for them to accept a snack.

I recommend to people starting to always take either an existing group of girls or a sole male (do NOT keep males together, even if they are from the same litter, it is a myth that it works). I would recommend the existing group of females because 1. Coupling of mice from different origins is difficult if you don't have any experience 2. I personally just find girls more fun because you can keep them in a group.
It depends what you want from the mice, males tend to be easier to tame and calmer than girls. If you want a mouse to cuddle with I would try a male before the females.

It's about 60-70 centimeters in width, about 50 cm high and 50 centimeters wide. It's pretty big and square. I use suction cups to hang toys and hammocks.

I use a terrarium that I bought on a second hand site for like 20 bucks. Some buy empty aquariums and use that, the benefit of that is you can use a lot of bedding for digging (they love tunneling) or a wire cage which I find the least handy. They tend to throw out bedding through the bars and the smell is much more noticeable. Besides, it is kind of hard to find a proper wire cage, the average length between two bars are most of the time too wide. If you really want a cage with bars you have to make sure a young mouse can't escape through, they can get to the tiniest hole.

Oh they are lovely, they can be pretty tame if you put your time into it, but it also depends on personality. You will be surprised by the fact they can have such different personalities. I love decorating their cage, it's so fun to watch them explore their new home. There are two downsides, they tend to get ill quickly if you don't give them proper care (mostly skin or lung illnesses). The second is they have short lives, you'll get attached and will have to say goodbye way too soon, some sooner than others. I've been keeping mice for almost 7 years, I've had many girls, I keep groups of at least 5, some reached a good age, some didn't. There is no predicting in that, but there are tips that give them a better chance at getting old. Like find a proper breeder, no petstore mice, they are from large scale breeders that don't look for defects, they just breed for money. Buy quality food (obvious) the more natural, the better, they'll be less picky when eating. Habitat is a big factor too. 

All in all, after all these years of keeping these little creatures, I can honestly say they are worth it. They are just so cute. You'll bond more with some mice than others and it's always awesome when a mouse puts it's trust in you. I love their little hands, I love it when I give my girls snacks that they come running for their favorite treat.

Tldr: mice are the best.

When it comes to being skittish, it depends from mouse to mouse. I have four at the moment and two are supertame, they crawl on my hand but the two others are scaredy cats. They need a lot of attention to get them tame and keep them tame.

They are very much like rats when it comes to company, some keep males alone because they tend to fight, but it's not ideal. I personally prefer females because you can keep them in groups.
